title: RESILIENCE
mv: For I know that my Redeemer lives, And He shall stand at last on the earth.
mvp: “For I know that my Redeemer lives, And He shall stand at last on the earth.” Job 19:25 (NKJV)
assignment: Identify two (2) recent situations where you felt discouraged, overwhelmed, or tempted to give up. For each setback, itemise: What happened, how you reacted and the lessons you learned (5X2=10 marks).

b.x: Resilience is the ability to bounce back from difficulties, adapt to challenges, and keep going despite setbacks. It is about inner strength, perseverance, and maintaining hope when life is hard. It is not just about enduring hardships but also thriving despite hardships (Genesis 26:18-22). Biblically, resilience is the strengthening of our faith through trials. Resilience plays a major role in our walk with God on earth. We will definitely come across fire, water and storms of life, and it is resilience that will keep us going irrespective of what we might face as we journey through life (Romans 8:35-39).

It is not the water around a ship that drowns it, but the water that enters the ship. To cultivate resilience, we must consciously choose to rely on God's strength and guidance through life's inevitable trials and difficulties and not allow it overwhelm us. We become resilient when we:

i: Focus on God’s word. Let the word of God guide and transform you. Seek to interpret circumstances in the light of God’s truth (Isaiah 43:2; John 17:17; Job 22:28; Mark 11:23).

Commit to consistent prayer. Prayer allows us to process emotions, seek guidance, and be honest before God. Depend on Him fully, do not rely on your understanding (1 Thessalonians 5:17; Proverbs 3:5-6).
See challenges as opportunities. Difficulties are not just obstacles; they are defining moments to build us. Ask God for wisdom to navigate trials rather than looking for escapes (James 1:2-4).

Draw strength from a faith community. Surround yourself with other believers who can encourage, support, and pray with you. Resilience is strengthened when shared within a faith community (Hebrews 10:24-25).
Analyse the current struggles correctly. Remember the temporary nature of difficulties and remain optimistic (Psalm 30:5; 2 Corinthians 4:17-18; Job 14:7-9; Jeremiah 29:11).

Care for yourself while serving others. Physical, emotional, and mental well-being are essential to resilience. Serving others not only blesses them but gives you insight and strength (Galatians 5:13).

b.x: The Bible has records of people who were resilient in the face of hardship:

i: Joseph overcame betrayal and hardship to fulfil God’s plan (Genesis 45:7-8).
Peter was steadfast in the face of persecution (Acts 5:25-29).
Paul faced trials, imprisonment, and rejection, yet he boldly continued in faith (2Corinthians 4:8-9).

b.x: Usually, enduring trials can lead to spiritual maturity and completeness (James 1:2-4). When this is done through faith, it can help refine character, build endurance and hope (Romans 5:3-5). Resilience helps us rely on God's power, which is made perfect in our weakness (2Corinthians 12:9; Isaiah 40:31). It helps us gain confidence in God's constant presence and guidance, even in challenging times (Isaiah 41:10; 43:2; Proverbs 3:5-6). It provides inner peace rooted in Christ's victory (John 16:33; Philippians 4:6-7). Resilience helps us understand that trials have a purpose within God's plan for the good of those who love Him (Romans 8:28).
Resilience is not merely "bouncing back," but a process of growth and transformation through faith.
